mainTopic: Who is not trusted to swear, what happens when both litigants are suspect, and whether an oath that cannot be taken 'returns to סיני' or makes the obligated person pay
overview: The amud opens by finishing a list of false oaths that make a person a חשוד על השבועה. It then explains that the משנה adds the dice player and similar people because they are disqualified מדרבנן, while the earlier cases are disqualified מדאורייתא. When both litigants are suspect, רבא asks רב נחמן which רבי holds which view and what the הלכה is. רב נחמן says he does not know, but a tradition reports that רבי יוסי says יחלוקו, and רב נחמן ruled that way in a real case. The גמרא then asks what 'the oath returned to its place' means. The Sages of בבל, identified as רב ושמואל, say it returns to סיני and the court does nothing; their proof is the rule that a person cannot pass an oath on to his sons. The Sages of ארץ ישראל, identified as רבי אבא, say it returns to the one obligated, who pays because he must swear but cannot, as shown in the story of the snatched metal. רבא supports רבי אבא from a ברייתא that the oath is 'between the two of them' and not between heirs, and the גמרא's working out of that case continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Closing the list of false oaths
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes the list of false oaths that make a person untrustworthy to swear, adding 'and anything similar to it.'
steps.simpleTranslation: And anything that is similar to it.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the last words of the previous discussion. The גמרא is closing its list of obviously false oaths by saying that any similar oath counts too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The list was not meant to be complete. Any oath that is clearly false, like the examples given before, also makes the person a חשוד על השבועה.

keyTerms.meaning: that is similar to it
a person suspected of swearing falsely, so he is not trusted to take an oath

phrases.english: And anything that is similar to it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the previous discussion of what makes someone a חשוד על השבועה.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Any oath that is obviously false, like the listed examples, disqualifies a person from swearing.

steps.title: Quoting the dice player case
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's case where one litigant is a dice player.
steps.simpleTranslation: If one of them was a dice player...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a line from the משנה about a litigant who plays dice for money. This sets up the question that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, when one side is a dice player or similar, the other side swears and collects. The גמרא brings this line only so it can ask about it.

keyTerms.meaning: one who plays dice for money (a gambler)

phrases.english: If one of them was
a dice player.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to a new line in the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If one litigant is a dice player, he is not trusted to swear, so the other side swears and collects.

steps.title: Why add more examples?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the משנה needs the dice player case when it already gave examples of people who are suspect to swear.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why do I need this as well?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what the dice player case adds. The משנה already taught about people who can't be trusted to swear.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה already covered people suspected on oaths. Adding the dice player and the others looks like extra, so the גמרא wants to know what new point they teach.

keyTerms.meaning: why do I need this further? (asking why something extra is taught)

phrases.english: Why do I need this as well?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about the משנה line quoted in step 2.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What the extra list of disqualified people teaches beyond the earlier case.

steps.title: Torah-level and rabbinic-level disqualification
steps.stepSummary: The משנה first teaches people disqualified by Torah law, then people disqualified by rabbinic law.
steps.simpleTranslation: It taught a disqualification from the Torah, and it also teaches a disqualification from the Rabbis.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains that the extra cases are a different kind of disqualification. They are rabbinic, not from the Torah.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Someone who swore falsely is disqualified מדאורייתא. A dice player, a lender with interest, and the others are disqualified מדרבנן. The משנה teaches that both kinds lose the right to swear.

keyTerms.meaning: a disqualification from Torah law
a disqualification from rabbinic law

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה lists two kinds of people not trusted to swear: those disqualified by the Torah and those disqualified by the Rabbis, like a dice player.

phrases.english: It taught a disqualification from the Torah,
and it also teaches a disqualification from the Rabbis.

steps.triggerLanguage: תְּנָא פְּסוּלָא דְּאוֹרָיְיתָא וְקָתָנֵי פְּסוּלָא דְּרַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 3.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The extra cases are not repeats; they are a second category, people disqualified only by rabbinic law.

steps.title: Quoting the case where both are suspect
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's case where both litigants are suspected of swearing falsely.
steps.simpleTranslation: If both of them were suspect...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next line of the משנה, where neither side can be trusted to swear. This sets up רבא's question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In our printed משנה, רבי יוסי says the oath 'returns to its place.' רבי מאיר says they split the money (יחלוקו). The גמרא is about to question which רבי said which.

keyTerms.meaning: both of them are suspect (on oaths)
the oath goes back to its place (the משנה's ruling for רבי יוסי in our printed text)

phrases.english: If both of them were suspect.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to the next case in the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Printed משנה: רבי יוסי says the oath returns to its place; רבי מאיר says they divide.

steps.title: רבא asks which version is correct
steps.stepSummary: רבא asks רב נחמן how the משנה is really taught, and רב נחמן says he does not know.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said to רב נחמן: How did we learn it? He said to him: I don't know.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא asks רב נחמן which opinion belongs to which רבי in the משנה. רב נחמן honestly answers that he does not know.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא is unsure whether רבי יוסי or רבי מאיר holds יחלוקו. רב נחמן does not have a clear tradition. Step 8 brings a tradition that answers this.

keyTerms.meaning: how did we learn it? (which version of the משנה is correct)
I don't know

steps.confusionAlert: רבא is not asking what the case is about. He is asking which רבי says which opinion, because the names may be switched.

phrases.english: רבא said to רב נחמן:
How did we learn it?
phrases.notes: He means: who in the משנה says 'the oath returns' and who says 'they split it'?

phrases.english: He said to him: I don't know.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רָבָא לְרַב נַחְמָן הֵיכִי תְּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the attribution of the opinions in the משנה quoted in step 5.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which רבי holds which opinion in the case where both are suspect.

steps.title: רבא asks what the הלכה is
steps.stepSummary: רבא then asks what the הלכה is, and again רב נחמן says he does not know.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the הלכה? He said to him: I don't know.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא asks a second question: what is the practical law? רב נחמן again says he does not know.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even without knowing who said what, a practical ruling would help. רב נחמן doesn't have that either. Steps 8 and 11 bring traditions that answer both questions.

keyTerms.meaning: what is the הלכה?

phrases.english: What is the halacha?
He said to him: I don't know.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A follow-up question after the first one was not answered.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The practical halacha when both litigants are suspect.

steps.title: A tradition: רבי יוסי says divide
steps.stepSummary: A tradition in רב נחמן's name says that רבי יוסי is the one who rules יחלוקו.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was stated: רב יוסף בר מניומי said in the name of רב נחמן: רבי יוסי says they divide.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a tradition that answers רבא's first question. It is רבי יוסי who says to split the money.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the reverse of our printed משנה, where רבי מאיר says יחלוקו. The same רב נחמן who said 'I don't know' is quoted here as holding that רבי יוסי says יחלוקו.

keyTerms.meaning: they divide (the disputed money)

phrases.english: It was stated:
רב יוסף בר מניומי said,
רב נחמן said:
רבי יוסי says: They divide.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיתְּמַר אָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף בַּר מִנְיוֹמֵי אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבא's unanswered question from step 6.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The opinion יחלוקו belongs to רבי יוסי.

steps.title: רב זביד teaches the same
steps.stepSummary: רב זביד בר אושעיא also teaches that רבי יוסי says יחלוקו.
steps.simpleTranslation: And so too, רב זביד בר אושעיא taught: רבי יוסי says they divide.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second source that agrees with the tradition in step 8.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A separate teacher has the same version, so it is not just one person's report. This makes it stronger that רבי יוסי is the one who says יחלוקו.

keyTerms.meaning: and so too it was taught (introduces support)

phrases.aramaic: וְכֵן תָּנֵי רַב זְבִיד בַּר אוֹשַׁעְיָא,
phrases.english: And so too, רב זביד בר אושעיא taught:
רבי יוסי says: They divide.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכֵן תָּנֵי רַב זְבִיד בַּר אוֹשַׁעְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the tradition of step 8 with a second source.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The teaching of רב זביד בר אושעיא.

steps.title: Another version of רב זביד's chain
steps.stepSummary: Some say רב זביד taught it in the name of רבי אושעיא, not as 'son of אושעיא'.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say: רב זביד taught in the name of רבי אושעיא: רבי יוסי says they divide.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second version of who passed down רב זביד's teaching. The content stays the same.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The only question is whether 'אושעיא' is רב זביד's father or a teacher he quotes. In both versions, רבי יוסי says יחלוקו.

phrases.english: There are those who say:

phrases.aramaic: תָּנֵי רַב זְבִיד אָמַר רַבִּי אוֹשַׁעְיָא,
phrases.english: רב זביד taught that רבי אושעיא said:
phrases.notes: Here אושעיא is a teacher רב זביד quotes, not his father as in the last line.

phrases.english: רבי יוסי says: They divide.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיכָּא דְּאָמְרִי תָּנֵי רַב זְבִיד אָמַר רַבִּי אוֹשַׁעְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different chain of names for the support in step 9.

steps.title: רב נחמן ruled to divide in a real case
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף בר מניומי reports that רב נחמן ruled יחלוקו in an actual case.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף בר מניומי said: רב נחמן made a ruling in a real case: they divide.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers רבא's second question about the הלכה. רב נחמן actually ruled in a real case that the two sides split the money.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A ruling in a real case (מעשה רב) shows what the practical הלכה is. When both litigants are suspect, they divide the disputed amount.

keyTerms.meaning: he made a ruling in a real case

steps.whatToRemember: When both sides are חשודים on oaths, the הלכה is יחלוקו: they split the money. The tradition says this is רבי יוסי's view, and רב נחמן ruled this way in practice.
steps.whyThisMatters: This settles the practical הלכה that רבא asked about in step 7, based on a real ruling and not only on theory.

phrases.english: רב יוסף בר מניומי said:
רב נחמן made a ruling in a real case:
They divide.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף בַּר מִנְיוֹמֵי עֲבַד רַב נַחְמָן עוֹבָדָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the halacha question of step 7 with a real ruling.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: In practice, when both litigants are suspect on oaths, they divide the disputed amount.

steps.title: What does 'the oath returned to its place' mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's phrase 'the oath returned to its place' and asks where exactly the oath 'returns' to.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'The oath returned to its place.' To where did it return?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the משנה's other ruling for the case where both sides are suspected of lying under oath. It asks what 'returned to its place' really means.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase is unclear. It could mean nobody swears and the court steps back. It could also mean the oath goes back to the person who first owed it, so he pays. The question sets up the two answers in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: To where?

phrases.english: The oath returned to its place.
phrases.notes: The משנה as we have it gives this to רבי יוסי, but by the tradition the גמרא just brought, it's רבי מאיר's view.

phrases.english: To where did it return?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the discussion of how to rule on יחלוקו and turns to explaining רבי יוסי's words.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The meaning of the phrase 'the oath returned to its place.'

steps.title: Two explanations: back to סיני, or back to the one who owed it
steps.stepSummary: רבי אמי reports that the Sages of בבל say the oath returns to סיני, while the Sages of ארץ ישראל say it returns to the one obligated to swear.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אמי said: Our Sages in בבל said the oath returned to סיני. Our Sages in ארץ ישראל said the oath returned to the one who was obligated in it.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אמי gives two different answers to the question. One comes from the Sages in בבל and one from the Sages in ארץ ישראל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Back to סיני' means the court takes no action. The case is left to Heaven, based on the oath at סיני to keep the Torah. 'Back to the one obligated' means the defendant, who owed the oath, cannot swear, so he must pay. These are two opposite outcomes.

keyTerms.meaning: Our Sages in בבל
Mount סיני, where the Jewish people swore to keep the Torah
The one who is obligated to take it (the oath)

steps.confusionAlert: 'Returns to סיני' does not mean someone swears at סיני. It means the court steps aside, and the matter is left to the oath already taken at סיני.

phrases.english: Rabbi Ami said:
Our Sages in Babylonia said:
The oath returned to Sinai,
phrases.notes: He means the oath everyone took at סיני to keep the Torah. The court does nothing, and Heaven will judge the liar.

phrases.english: Our Sages in Eretz Yisrael said:
The oath returned to the one who was obligated in it.
phrases.notes: Since that person cannot swear, he loses and has to pay.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אַמֵּי, רַבּוֹתֵינוּ שֶׁבְּבָבֶל אָמְרוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 12.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Either the oath returns to סיני (the court does nothing), or it returns to the one who owed it (he pays).

steps.title: רב פפא names the Sages behind each view
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא says 'our Sages in בבל' are רב ושמואל, and 'our Sages in ארץ ישראל' is רבי אבא.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: 'Our Sages in בבל' are רב ושמואל. 'Our Sages in ארץ ישראל' is רבי אבא.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא tells us who exactly is meant by the two unnamed groups of Sages. He will now prove each identification.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אמי only said 'our Sages' without names. רב פפא connects each view to known Sages, based on their rulings elsewhere. The next steps bring those rulings as proof.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said:
'Our Sages in Babylonia' are Rav and Shmuel;
'Our Sages in Eretz Yisrael' is Rabbi Abba.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא: רַבּוֹתֵינוּ שֶׁבְּבָבֶל – רַב וּשְׁמוּאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Identifies who holds the two views quoted in step 13.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The view 'back to סיני' belongs to רב ושמואל. The view 'back to the one obligated' belongs to רבי אבא.

steps.title: Background for the proof: orphans collecting from orphans
steps.stepSummary: To prove the view of רב ושמואל, the גמרא quotes the משנה that orphans collect only with an oath. It explains that this means orphans collecting from the borrower's orphans.
steps.simpleTranslation: That 'our Sages in בבל' are רב ושמואל we see from what we learned: 'Likewise, orphans collect only with an oath.' We asked: from whom? If from the borrower himself, that makes no sense. Their father would collect without an oath, and they would need one?! Rather, it means: orphans collecting from orphans collect only with an oath.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins its proof about רב ושמואל. First it sets up the background: a משנה about orphans, and how that משנה must be understood.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Orphans should not have it worse than their father. So the משנה cannot mean they need an oath to collect from a living borrower. It must mean the lender's orphans collecting from the borrower's orphans. This background prepares for רב ושמואל's ruling in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: Orphans (here, children who inherited after a parent died)
They collect payment only with an oath
And we discussed it
If you say
Borrower

phrases.english: 'Our Sages in Babylonia' are Rav and Shmuel:
as we learned: And likewise orphans
collect payment only with an oath.
And we discussed it: from whom?
If you say from the borrower,
their father would take payment without an oath,
and they need an oath?!
Rather, this is what it is saying:
And likewise orphans, from orphans,
collect payment only with an oath.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins proving the first identification made in step 14.
steps.raayaObject: That רב ושמואל hold the oath 'returns to סיני.'
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה about orphans collecting only with an oath, read as orphans collecting from orphans.

steps.title: רב and שמואל: a person cannot pass an oath on to his sons
steps.stepSummary: רב ושמואל limit the משנה to a lender who died before the borrower. If the borrower died first, the lender already owed an oath, and his sons cannot swear in his place, so they collect nothing.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ושמואל both say: This was taught only when the lender died while the borrower was alive. But if the borrower died while the lender was alive, the lender already became obligated to swear to the borrower's sons. A person cannot pass on an oath to his sons.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the heart of the proof. רב ושמואל rule that when the required oath cannot be taken, the lender's sons get nothing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the borrower died, the lender could only collect from the orphans by swearing. His sons cannot take their father's oath, so the debt is not collected, and the court does nothing. This matches 'the oath returns to סיני.'

keyTerms.meaning: They taught this only in a case where
Lender
A person cannot pass on an oath to his sons
Both of them

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the famous rule of אין אדם מוריש שבועה לבניו. It shows that when no one can swear, the court simply does not take money away.

phrases.english: And Rav and Shmuel both say:
They taught this only
where the lender died during the borrower's lifetime;
but if the borrower died during the lender's lifetime,

phrases.aramaic: כְּבָר נִתְחַיֵּיב מַלְוֶה לִבְנֵי לֹוֶה שְׁבוּעָה,
phrases.english: the lender already became obligated to swear to the borrower's sons,
and a person cannot pass on an oath to his sons.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַב וּשְׁמוּאֵל דְּאָמְרִי תַּרְוַיְיהוּ: לֹא שָׁנוּ אֶלָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the proof begun in step 15 by bringing רב ושמואל's ruling on that משנה.
steps.raayaObject: רב ושמואל hold that the oath 'returns to סיני.'
steps.raayaSupportSource: Their ruling that when the lender's oath cannot be taken, his sons collect nothing.

steps.title: A story to show רבי אבא's view: the snatched metal
steps.stepSummary: To prove רבי אבא's view, the גמרא starts a story. A man snatched a metal piece from another. There was one witness, and the snatcher admitted it but claimed the metal was his.
steps.simpleTranslation: That 'our Sages in ארץ ישראל' is רבי אבא we see from a story. A man snatched a piece of metal from his fellow. The case came before רב אמי, and רבי אבא was sitting before him. The victim brought one witness that the man snatched it. The snatcher said: 'Yes, I snatched it, but I snatched what is mine.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a court story to prove that רבי אבא holds the oath returns to the one who owed it. Here it only lays out the facts; the ruling comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is one witness, which normally obligates the defendant to swear. But the snatcher admits he took the metal by force, which raises a problem with letting him swear. These facts set up רבי אבא's ruling, which will come next.

keyTerms.meaning: He snatched (grabbed by force)
A piece of cast metal
A witness
And I snatched what is mine

phrases.english: 'Our Sages in Eretz Yisrael' is Rabbi Abba:
as there was a certain man
who snatched a piece of metal from his fellow;
he came before Rav Ami,
phrases.notes: 'He' is the victim, who came to court to get the metal back.

phrases.english: and Rabbi Abba was sitting before him.
He brought one witness
that he did indeed snatch it from him.
He said to him: 'Yes, I snatched it,'
phrases.notes: Now the snatcher is the one speaking.

phrases.english: 'but I snatched what is mine.'

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבּוֹתֵינוּ שֶׁבְּאֶרֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵל רַבִּי אַבָּא – דְּהָהוּא גַּבְרָא דַּחֲטַף נְסָכָא מֵחַבְרֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns from proving רב ושמואל's view to proving the second identification of step 14, רבי אבא.
steps.raayaObject: רבי אבא holds the oath 'returns to the one obligated in it.'
steps.raayaSupportSource: A case judged before רב אמי in which רבי אבא was present (the ruling follows).

steps.title: רבי אמי asks how judges can rule on the snatched metal
steps.stepSummary: רבי אמי asks how a court could rule in the snatching case, since all three options seem wrong.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אמי said: How should judges rule in this case? Should they tell him 'Go pay'? There aren't two witnesses. Should they let him go free? There is one witness. Should they tell him 'Go swear'? Since he said 'I snatched it,' he is like a robber.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אמי lays out the problem in the snatching story: every normal ruling seems wrong. This sets up רבי אבא's answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A court needs two witnesses to make someone pay, so 'pay' fails. One witness is enough to force an oath, so 'go free' fails. But the usual oath against one witness is not allowed here, because the man admitted snatching, which makes him like a גזלן, and a גזלן is not trusted to swear.

keyTerms.meaning: Judges
Two witnesses; needed to force payment
One witness; can only force an oath
Robber; not trusted to take an oath

steps.confusionAlert: The snatcher is not being called a full robber by proven testimony. He is only 'like' a גזלן because he admits grabbing the object and has no proof it is his.

phrases.english: Rabbi Ami said:
How should judges rule in this case?
Should they say to him, 'Go pay'?
There are not two witnesses.
Should they let him go free?
There is one witness.
Should they say to him, 'Go take an oath'?
Since he said, 'I did snatch it,'
he is like a robber.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the story begun in Step 17 by asking how to rule in it.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What ruling fits a case where payment, exemption, and an oath all seem impossible.

steps.title: רבי אבא: one who must swear but cannot, pays
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבא rules that the snatcher is obligated to swear but cannot, and so he must pay.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבא said to him: He is obligated to swear but cannot swear, and anyone who is obligated to swear but cannot swear must pay.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבא answers רבי אמי's question: the snatcher pays. This is the proof the גמרא promised for רבי אבא's view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The one witness creates an oath obligation, but the snatcher is disqualified from swearing. רבי אבא does not drop the oath; it stays with the defendant, and since he cannot swear, he loses and pays. This shows that for רבי אבא the oath 'returns to the one obligated', not 'to סיני'.

keyTerms.meaning: Someone obligated to take an oath
And cannot take the oath
Pays

steps.whatToRemember: The rule מחויב שבועה ואינו יכול לישבע משלם: if you owe an oath but cannot take it, you pay. This is רבי אבא's position, matching 'the oath returns to the one obligated'.
steps.whyThisMatters: This principle is a well-known rule in monetary law and is the core of רבי אבא's side in the dispute from Step 13.

phrases.english: Rabbi Abba said to him:
He is obligated to take an oath
and cannot take an oath,
and anyone who is obligated to take an oath
and cannot take an oath must pay.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי אמי's question from Step 18.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The snatcher pays, because he is obligated to swear and cannot.

steps.title: רבא supports רבי אבא from a teaching about heirs
steps.stepSummary: רבא says רבי אבא's view makes sense, based on a ברייתא that the oath is 'between the two of them' and not between heirs.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: It makes sense like רבי אבא, since רבי אמי teaches: 'The oath of ה׳ shall be between the two of them' — and not between the heirs.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא brings a source to back רבי אבא. He quotes a ברייתא that says the oath of the פסוק applies only to the original two parties, not to their heirs.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא learns from the words 'between the two of them' that heirs are not part of this oath. רבא will try to show that this only makes sense if a lost oath leads to payment, as רבי אבא holds. Notice that the source comes from רבי אמי himself, who raised the problem in Step 18.

keyTerms.meaning: It makes sense / it is logical
The oath of ה׳ (from the פסוק)
Heirs

phrases.english: Rava said:
It makes sense like Rabbi Abba,
since Rabbi Ami teaches:
'The oath of ה׳ shall be between the two of them'
— and not between the heirs.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a supporting source for the view רבי אבא expressed in Step 19.
steps.raayaObject: רבי אבא's view that an oath that cannot be taken leads to payment.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא taught by רבי אמי on the פסוק 'שבועת ה' תהיה בין שניהם'.

steps.title: What case is the heirs teaching about?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what case the ברייתא means, and suggests: the lender's son claims 100, and the borrower's son admits 50.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the case? If you say that he told him, 'My father had a hundred in your father's hands,' and he answered, 'He owed fifty and did not owe fifty'—
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what situation the ברייתא is describing. It offers a first suggestion, which it will test in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: To use the ברייתא as proof, we must know exactly when heirs are freed from an oath. The first idea is a classic partial admission (מודה במקצת) between the two sons. This is only a proposal; it is set up to be checked.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the case? What are the circumstances?
If you say (introduces a suggestion that may be rejected)
A hundred (זוז / dinars)

phrases.english: What is the case?
If you say that he said to him:
phrases.notes: The speaker is the lender's son, talking to the borrower's son.

phrases.english: 'My father had a hundred in your father's hands,'
and he said to him:
'He has fifty, and fifty he does not have'
phrases.notes: Meaning: my father owed yours fifty, but not the other fifty.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the exact case behind the ברייתא quoted in Step 20.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The specific case where heirs are exempt from the oath.

steps.title: That case cannot be it: the son is just like his father
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the first suggestion: in that case there is no difference between the son and his father.
steps.simpleTranslation: What difference is it to me whether it is him or his father?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on its own suggestion. In that case the son should have to swear just like his father would.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The borrower's son is speaking with certainty: he admits fifty and denies fifty. That is a normal partial admission, and he can swear on it just like his father could. So this case gives no reason to exempt heirs, and the ברייתא must be talking about something else.

keyTerms.term: מָה לִי הוּא וּמָה לִי אֲבוּהָא
keyTerms.meaning: What difference is it whether it is him or his father?

phrases.english: What difference is it to me whether it is him
phrases.notes: 'Him' is the borrower's son who is now being sued.

phrases.english: or his father?

steps.triggerLanguage: מָה לִי הוּא וּמָה לִי אֲבוּהָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the case proposed in Step 21.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the proposed case for the ברייתא, not רבא's overall proof.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: In that case the son claims with certainty, so he can swear just as his father could; nothing about being an heir changes the oath.

steps.title: A new case: the heir knows about fifty but not the other fifty
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests the ברייתא is talking about a case where the borrower's son admits 50 and says he does not know about the other 50.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, isn't the case like this? The lender's son said to the borrower's son: "My father had 100 coins in your father's hands." The borrower's son answered: "I know about fifty, but I don't know about the other fifty."
steps.whatsHappening: The first reading of the ברייתא was rejected. Now the גמרא offers a different case, and this one is the setup רבא needs to prove רבי אבא's ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the rejected case, the son answered with confidence, just as his father would have. Here the son says "I don't know" about part of the claim, and the ברייתא frees heirs from the oath in a case like this. That implies the original borrower, who admits fifty but is unsure about the rest, would owe an oath he cannot take and so would pay, just as רבי אבא rules. The גמרא spells this out on the next amud.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, is it not that... (the גמרא offers a better reading after rejecting one)
A sum of 100 coins (זוז)
I know
I do not know
Someone who admits to part of a claim and must swear on the rest

steps.confusionAlert: The son is not saying "I don't owe the other fifty." He is saying "I don't know." That is why he cannot swear: an oath needs certain knowledge.
steps.whyThisMatters: This case links the ברייתא's rule about heirs to רבי אבא's idea of someone who owes an oath but cannot take it.

phrases.english: Rather, is it not that he said to him:
phrases.notes: "He" is the lender's son, speaking to the borrower's son.

phrases.english: "My father had a hundred in your father's hands,"
he said to him:
"Fifty I know about,
and fifty I do not know about"?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the case rejected in Step 22 with a new case that fits רבא's proof.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which case is the ברייתא talking about when it says the oath does not pass to heirs?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The heir admits fifty but says he does not know about the other fifty. The ברייתא exempts him only because he is an heir. This implies the original borrower in this position would owe an oath he cannot take, and would pay.
